title: Prefix Sums
summary: Build cumulative totals, then answer ranges with two lookups

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: range_sums(values, queries) returns sums for half-open ranges [left, right). Build a prefix table once, then watch each query cancel the part before left.

idea: prefix[i] is the total before i. The extra zero handles ranges beginning at zero and empty ranges. Trace the table being built, then compare the two boundaries for each query.

title: Monotonic Stack
summary: Resolve waiting days as a warmer temperature arrives

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: warmer_days(temperatures) gives the number of days until a strictly warmer day, or zero. Use pending indices to avoid restarting a search for every day.

idea: The pending stack stores indices whose warmer day has not arrived. Each index enters and leaves once. Equal temperatures stay pending because the question asks for a strictly warmer day.

title: Topological Sort
summary: Release tasks as their final prerequisite is removed

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: task_order(graph) returns any valid prerequisite-first order, or None for a cycle. graph maps every node to outgoing neighbours; every neighbour is a key.

idea: Indegree counts prerequisites that remain. Removing a ready task reduces the counts of its dependants. If no task is ready but some remain, a cycle blocks the schedule.

title: 0/1 Knapsack
summary: Fill a capacity table without taking an item twice

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: pack(items, capacity) returns the maximum value of items that fit. Each (weight, value) item may be taken once; weights are positive and values nonnegative.

idea: The table records the best value at each capacity. Iterate capacity downward so each transition reads a state that has not used the current item. Trace upward updates to see why they would solve an unbounded problem instead.

title: Bellman–Ford
summary: Relax weighted edges and detect reachable negative cycles

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: shortest(n, edges, start) returns distances for nodes 0..n-1, using float("inf") for unreachable nodes. Each edge is (from, to, weight). Return None if a negative cycle is reachable from start.

idea: One full pass can extend a shortest route by another edge. A simple path has at most n-1 edges. Any reachable edge that can still improve a distance after those passes proves a reachable negative cycle; an unreachable cycle must not invalidate the result.

title: Edit Distance Rows
summary: Compare prefixes with insertion, deletion and substitution

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: distance(a, b) returns the fewest single-character insertions, deletions and substitutions turning a into b. Keep only the previous row and the current row.

idea: Each cell compares two prefixes. Above means delete, left means insert, and the diagonal means match or substitute. Two rows are enough because older rows are never read again.

title: Linear Regression
summary: Move a fitted line by following the mean squared-error gradient

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: fit(xs, ys, steps, rate) begins at w=b=0 and returns (w, b) after steps of gradient descent on mean squared error. Compute both gradients from the old parameters; include the factor 2/n.

idea: The gradient tells which parameter direction increases loss. Subtracting it moves downhill. Watch the fitted line and loss curve; a large learning rate can overshoot even when the derivatives are correct.

title: Logistic Regression
summary: Turn a score into a probability and learn a binary boundary

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: fit(xs, ys, steps, rate) starts w=b=0 and returns (w, b). Use sigmoid(w*x+b) and gradients mean((p-y)*x), mean(p-y) for binary cross-entropy. Inputs in this lab have moderate scores.

idea: The sigmoid maps a real score into (0,1). For binary cross-entropy its derivative with respect to the score is p-y. The trace shows the parameters and mean squared probability residual as a diagnostic, not as the optimized loss.

title: Nearest Neighbours
summary: Rank points by distance, then vote with explicit tie rules

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: nearest_label(points, labels, query, k) classifies numeric vectors. Equal distances preserve training order; a tied vote chooses the smaller integer label. k is positive and training data is nonempty.

idea: Squared distance has the same ordering as Euclidean distance. The trace keeps distances, selected indices and votes visible. Feature scales change which points are neighbours; stable tie rules make the outcome reproducible.

title: Decision Stumps
summary: Try thresholds and choose the lowest weighted Gini impurity

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: best_split(values, labels) returns the midpoint between consecutive distinct sorted values with the lowest weighted Gini impurity. Equal scores choose the smaller threshold. Return None when fewer than two distinct values exist.

idea: A split is useful when it leaves purer groups. Weight each group by its size, then compare candidate midpoints. Scanning thresholds in ascending order and accepting only a lower score gives a deterministic smallest-threshold tie break.

title: Train-only Standardization
summary: Fit the centre and population deviation on training values only.
idea: Fit the centre and population deviation on training values only. Reuse both statistics for validation; a constant training column uses scale one.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: normalize(train, values) returns values standardized with the training mean and population standard deviation. train is nonempty. Use scale 1 for a constant column.

title: Confusion Matrix
summary: Rows are actual labels and columns are predicted labels.
idea: Rows are actual labels and columns are predicted labels. Trace each sample into its cell, including mistakes hidden by accuracy.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: confusion(actual, predicted, classes) returns a classes by classes count matrix. Labels are integers from 0 to classes-1; input lengths match.

title: Precision, Recall & F1
summary: Count true positives before dividing.
idea: Count true positives before dividing. A zero denominator returns zero; accuracy alone hides an imbalanced classifier.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: prf(actual, predicted) returns (precision, recall, F1) for binary 0/1 labels. For each undefined ratio return 0.0.

title: Threshold Sweep
summary: One score can produce different decisions.
idea: One score can produce different decisions. Compare F1 at candidate thresholds on validation labels; break equal scores toward the smaller threshold.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: choose_threshold(scores, labels, candidates) returns the candidate with greatest binary F1, choosing the smallest on a tie. A score >= threshold predicts 1; candidates is nonempty.

title: Cross-validation Folds
summary: Partition indices without loss or overlap.
idea: Partition indices without loss or overlap. Earlier folds receive the remainder; every validation item is excluded from its training fold.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: folds(n, k) returns k (training_indices, validation_indices) pairs with consecutive validation blocks. 1 <= k <= n. Put extra items in the earliest folds.

title: Ridge Regression
summary: A closed-form one-feature ridge fit shrinks the slope.
idea: A closed-form one-feature ridge fit shrinks the slope. Centre the data so the intercept is not penalized; lambda zero recovers least squares.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: ridge(xs, ys, penalty) returns (slope, intercept) minimizing sum squared error + penalty*slope**2. Inputs are nonempty and penalty >= 0. Return slope zero when the denominator is zero.

title: Numerical Gradient Check
summary: Compare a supplied gradient with central finite differences.
idea: Compare a supplied gradient with central finite differences. A deliberately wrong derivative must produce a visible error, rather than passing because training loss happens to fall.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: gradient_error(x, epsilon, derivative) returns abs(derivative - numerical_gradient) for f(x)=x**3-2*x. Use the central difference; epsilon > 0.

title: Adam Optimizer
summary: Follow first and second moment estimates, then correct their initial bias.
idea: Follow first and second moment estimates, then correct their initial bias. This is a scalar teaching implementation with epsilon outside the square root.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: adam_step(w, gradient, m, v, t, lr, beta1, beta2, epsilon) returns (new_w, new_m, new_v). t starts at 1 and epsilon > 0. Apply bias correction to both moments.

title: Mini-batch SGD
summary: Each batch updates the parameter before the next batch is evaluated.
idea: Each batch updates the parameter before the next batch is evaluated. Average within a batch, including a shorter final batch.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: epoch(xs, ys, w, lr, batch_size) returns the new scalar w after one ordered epoch minimizing mean squared error for y=w*x, with no intercept. Use gradient 2*mean((w*x-y)*x). batch_size > 0.

title: Multinomial Naive Bayes
summary: Count tokens per class with Laplace smoothing.
idea: Count tokens per class with Laplace smoothing. Work in log space to avoid multiplying tiny probabilities; repeated tokens contribute repeatedly.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: log_scores(documents, labels, query, vocabulary) returns log posterior scores (without normalization) for classes 0 and 1. Both classes have documents; vocabulary is nonempty and unique. Ignore query tokens outside vocabulary, use alpha=1 and empirical class priors.

title: PCA by Power Iteration
summary: Centre a two-dimensional cloud, build its covariance matrix and repeatedly multiply a direction.
idea: Centre a two-dimensional cloud, build its covariance matrix and repeatedly multiply a direction. The final unit vector points along the greatest variance; choose a consistent sign.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: principal_axis(points, steps) returns the first principal unit direction for 2D points using power iteration starting at (1,1)/sqrt(2). Centre points, use population covariance, take steps iterations; fall back to the covariance column with the greatest norm if the starting direction is orthogonal; return (0,0) for zero variance and orient x >= 0. Inputs are nonempty.

title: Silhouette Clustering Score
summary: A cluster assignment can be compact yet poorly separated.
idea: A cluster assignment can be compact yet poorly separated. Compare each point’s mean distance within its cluster with the nearest other cluster; singletons score zero.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: silhouette(points, labels) returns the mean silhouette for 1D points using absolute distance. There are at least two nonempty clusters. A singleton has score 0; if a=b=0 also use 0.

title: Stable Softmax & Temperature
summary: Subtract the largest logit before exponentiating.
idea: Subtract the largest logit before exponentiating. Temperature changes concentration without changing rank, and equal scores share probability.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: softmax(logits, temperature) returns normalized probabilities for finite logits and temperature > 0. Return [] for empty input. Avoid overflow for large logits.

title: Scaled Dot-product Attention
summary: A query scores keys; stable softmax turns scores into weights, then a weighted sum mixes values.
idea: A query scores keys; stable softmax turns scores into weights, then a weighted sum mixes values. Inspect scores, weights and the output vector.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: attend(query, keys, values) returns one attention output vector using dot products divided by sqrt(len(query)), followed by stable softmax. keys is nonempty, dimensions match, each value has the same width.

title: Causal Attention Mask
summary: An autoregressive position may read its prefix, including itself, but never later tokens.
idea: An autoregressive position may read its prefix, including itself, but never later tokens. Mask before softmax and normalize each allowed row.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: causal_weights(scores) takes a square nonempty score matrix and returns row softmax with columns j > i set to probability zero. Use stable exponentials over the unmasked prefix.

title: Nucleus Sampling Candidates
summary: Sort by probability and retain the smallest prefix reaching top-p mass.
idea: Sort by probability and retain the smallest prefix reaching top-p mass. Return renormalized candidates, with original index breaking ties. No random draw is hidden in this lab.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: nucleus(probabilities, p) returns (token_index, renormalized_probability) pairs. Nonnegative probabilities sum to one, 0 < p <= 1; sort descending, break ties by index, stop when cumulative mass reaches p (tolerance 1e-12).

title: Beam Search
summary: Greedy search discards every alternative immediately.
idea: Greedy search discards every alternative immediately. Keep a bounded set of complete prefixes, sum log probabilities and prune globally after each step.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: beam_search(transitions, start, steps, width) returns the highest log-score token path (including start) after exactly steps expansions. transitions maps a token to (next_token, probability) pairs; all expanded tokens have successors and probabilities > 0. Keep width paths; ties use lexicographic path order.

title: Byte-pair Merge Step
summary: A BPE training step counts adjacent token pairs, chooses the most frequent, then merges non-overlapping occurrences left to right.
idea: A BPE training step counts adjacent token pairs, chooses the most frequent, then merges non-overlapping occurrences left to right. This is a token-string teaching model, not a production tokenizer.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: merge_pair(tokens) returns (new_tokens, selected_pair) after one BPE merge. Ties choose the lexicographically smallest pair; joining concatenates token strings. With fewer than two tokens, return (a copy, None).

title: Cosine Retrieval
summary: Vector length should not dominate relevance.
idea: Vector length should not dominate relevance. Normalize dot products by both norms, give zero vectors score zero, and keep stable indices for tied documents.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: rank_vectors(query, documents, k) returns the top k document indices by descending cosine similarity, breaking ties by smaller index. Empty or zero vectors score 0. Dimensions match and k >= 0.

title: Layer Normalization
summary: Normalize within one token’s feature vector, using population variance and epsilon inside the square root.
idea: Normalize within one token’s feature vector, using population variance and epsilon inside the square root. Learned gain and bias then restore useful scale.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: layer_norm(values, gain, bias, epsilon) returns per-feature gain*(x-mean)/sqrt(variance+epsilon)+bias. Inputs are nonempty with matching widths; epsilon > 0.

title: Split identities before splitting examples
summary: Implement group_folds(groups,k) returning k lists of row indices.
idea: The split unit should match the deployment question. Group separation estimates new-group performance; it does not estimate future drift within groups, so a time-aware design may also be required.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: Implement group_folds(groups,k) returning k lists of row indices. Sort distinct group names and assign group number modulo k. Require 2<=k<=number of distinct groups.

title: Purge a gap before a temporal validation window
summary: Implement temporal_split(times,start,end,gap) returning (train_indices,validation_indices), preserving row order.
idea: A temporal split must be combined with point-in-time feature joins and train-only preprocessing. Time order alone does not prevent using a feature published after the prediction timestamp.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: Implement temporal_split(times,start,end,gap) returning (train_indices,validation_indices), preserving row order. Train if t<start-gap; validate if start<=t<=end. Require start<=end and gap>=0.

title: Treat tied ranking scores explicitly in ROC AUC
summary: Implement roc_auc(labels,scores) for equal nonempty lists, binary integer labels and finite scores.
idea: The quadratic reference is transparent for tiny evaluation fixtures. Large datasets should use a tie-aware rank algorithm. A high AUC can coexist with poor calibration or unacceptable errors at the chosen threshold.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: Implement roc_auc(labels,scores) for equal nonempty lists, binary integer labels and finite scores. Compute exact positive-negative pair credit, half for ties. Reject single-class data.

title: Compute average precision at tied score boundaries
summary: Implement average_precision(labels,scores).
idea: Average precision depends on prevalence and the evaluation population. Compare models on the same test population and retain class counts; a number alone does not establish business value.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: Implement average_precision(labels,scores). Group equal scores descending, accumulate TP and seen count, and sum (new positives/total positives)*precision at each group. Return 0 with no positives; validate nonempty equal lengths, binary labels and finite scores.

title: Measure probability error instead of only decisions
summary: Implement brier(labels,probabilities), validating equal nonempty sequences, binary integer labels and finite probabilities in [0,1].
idea: A proper scoring rule rewards truthful probabilities in expectation, but finite test scores still have uncertainty. Use held-out calibration data and avoid choosing a calibrator on the final test set.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: Implement brier(labels,probabilities), validating equal nonempty sequences, binary integer labels and finite probabilities in [0,1]. Return mean squared probability error.

title: Estimate calibration with explicit bin semantics
summary: Implement ece(labels,probs,bins) using equal-width bins [i/bins,(i+1)/bins), with 1 in the last.
idea: ECE depends on discretization and sample size. Treat it as an inspectable diagnostic rather than a calibrated confidence interval or a substitute for a proper scoring rule.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: Implement ece(labels,probs,bins) using equal-width bins [i/bins,(i+1)/bins), with 1 in the last. Validate binary labels, finite [0,1] probabilities, equal nonempty lengths and positive integer bins.

title: Report uncertainty for a measured success rate
summary: Implement wilson(successes,total,z=1.96) returning lower,upper.
idea: The z value determines the nominal confidence level through a normal approximation. Independence and representative sampling matter more than the number of decimals printed in the interval.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: Implement wilson(successes,total,z=1.96) returning lower,upper. Require integer 0<=successes<=total, total>0, and finite z>0. Clamp floating roundoff to [0,1].

title: Adjust a family of discoveries without losing original order
summary: Implement bh_adjust(pvalues) returning BH adjusted values in original order, capped at 1.
idea: BH controls a false-discovery rate under conditions such as independent or suitable positively dependent tests. It does not establish a causal effect or replace a predeclared experiment and a meaningful effect-size threshold.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: Implement bh_adjust(pvalues) returning BH adjusted values in original order, capped at 1. Accept empty input. Reject nonfinite values or values outside [0,1].

title: Join only features available at prediction time
summary: Implement asof_values(events,queries).
idea: Point-in-time correctness is a data-lineage property, not just a split choice. Backfills should preserve availability history so offline experiments can reconstruct what the online system actually knew.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: Implement asof_values(events,queries). Events are (entity,event_time,available_time,value); queries are (entity,time). Return latest eligible value ordered by (event_time,available_time), or None. No mutation; ties with identical timestamp pairs are outside this contract.

title: Fit residual trees in a tiny gradient-boosted regressor
summary: Implement fit_boost(x,y,rounds,rate) and predict_boost(model,x).
idea: A trainable baseline makes every later gain measurable. This tiny learner demonstrates gradient boosting correctly, while production libraries add numerical, categorical, performance and distributed engineering that must be evaluated separately.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: Implement fit_boost(x,y,rounds,rate) and predict_boost(model,x). Fit a mean baseline, then squared-error optimal residual stumps at midpoints of distinct x; ties choose smallest cut. Model is dict base, rate, stumps (cut,left,right). Constant x uses a constant residual stump with cut=inf. Validate nonempty equal finite data, rounds>=0 integer, 0<rate<=1.

title: Measure binned drift with smoothing and fixed boundaries
summary: Implement psi(reference,current,epsilon=1e-6) for equal nonempty nonnegative finite bin counts with positive totals.
idea: Smoothing reduces instability but changes the estimate, especially on tiny windows. PSI thresholds are not universal laws; calibrate alerts against reference variation and observed model outcomes.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: Implement psi(reference,current,epsilon=1e-6) for equal nonempty nonnegative finite bin counts with positive totals. Add epsilon to every bin count before normalizing each histogram; return sum((q-p)*log(q/p)). Require finite epsilon>0.

title: Use the finite-sample conformal rank
summary: Implement conformal_radius(residuals,alpha) with finite nonnegative residuals, nonempty input and 0<alpha<1.
idea: The guarantee depends on exchangeable calibration and future scores. An infinite interval honestly reports insufficient calibration information at the requested error level rather than silently overstating confidence.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: Implement conformal_radius(residuals,alpha) with finite nonnegative residuals, nonempty input and 0<alpha<1. Return sorted residual at one-based rank ceil((n+1)*(1-alpha)); return inf if rank>n.

title: Fuse retriever rankings without comparing incompatible scores
summary: Implement rrf(rankings,k=60) returning all ids sorted by descending sum 1/(k+rank), then id.
idea: RRF uses ranking evidence instead of uncalibrated score scales. Tune and evaluate it on representative relevance judgments, keeping final evaluation queries separate from parameter selection.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: Implement rrf(rankings,k=60) returning all ids sorted by descending sum 1/(k+rank), then id. Rank unique ids within each list starting at 1, ignoring repeated appearances without consuming another rank. Require k>0.

title: Chunk token identities without losing the tail
summary: Implement token_windows(tokens,size,overlap) returning (start,list_of_tokens) windows.
idea: Offsets make chunks auditable against the original token sequence. They must be mapped to the original source through a real tokenizer before showing quotations or citations to a user.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: Implement token_windows(tokens,size,overlap) returning (start,list_of_tokens) windows. Require integer size>0 and 0<=overlap<size. Advance by size-overlap and stop once the last emitted window reaches the end. Empty input returns [].

title: Reserve output space before adding retrieval context
summary: Implement pack_context(chunks,window,fixed,output).
idea: The allocator enforces the supplied accounting contract. Incorrect tokenizer counts or omitted tool/message formatting overhead can still overflow a model context window, so the final serialized request needs a separate budget check.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: Implement pack_context(chunks,window,fixed,output). chunks are (id,token_count), already ranked. Return admitted ids and total used context tokens. Skip oversized chunks, deduplicate admitted ids, require nonnegative integer counts/budgets and fixed+output<=window.

title: Evaluate retrieval with relevance and rank
summary: Implement retrieval_metrics(ranked,relevant,k) returning dict recall,mrr.
idea: Retrieval metrics evaluate the judged identifiers and ordering. They do not establish answer faithfulness, citation correctness or resistance to prompt injection; those require separate evaluation cases.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: Implement retrieval_metrics(ranked,relevant,k) returning dict recall,mrr. Deduplicate ranked preserving order, then take k. mrr is reciprocal first relevant rank or 0. No relevant ids gives None values. Require k>=1 integer.

title: Reject citations outside the supplied evidence set
summary: Implement citation_errors(claims,allowed).
idea: Identifier validation proves only that a reference belongs to the supplied set. Faithfulness needs a separate check against the referenced content, and uncertain claims should remain qualified rather than acquiring false certainty from a valid citation id.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: Implement citation_errors(claims,allowed). Each claim has text and citations list. Return ordered strings "i:missing" if no citations and "i:unknown:key" for each distinct unknown id in that claim, preserving first occurrence. Empty claims return [].

title: Filter retrieval permissions before selecting context
summary: Implement authorized_topk(docs,tenant,roles,k).
idea: Authorization must precede data disclosure. This local policy tests access filtering; it does not claim that role checks detect prompt injection or that a model will obey instructions once untrusted text enters its context.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: Implement authorized_topk(docs,tenant,roles,k). Each doc has id,tenant,roles (empty means tenant-public),score,text. Keep same-tenant docs whose roles intersect caller roles or are empty; rank by descending score then id; return at most k ids. Reject k<0. Do not mutate docs.

title: Authorize a tool call outside the model
summary: Implement tool_allowed(call,tenant,scopes,policy).
idea: The executor owns authorization. This deliberately small policy does not implement a full identity system, object ACLs or human confirmation; each must be supplied by trusted application infrastructure, never inferred from model output.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: Implement tool_allowed(call,tenant,scopes,policy). call has tool,tenant. policy maps tool->required scope. Return True only for a known tool, matching tenant and granted required scope; missing fields fail closed.

title: Stop an agent loop before exceeding its execution budget
summary: Implement admitted_steps(costs,max_steps,max_tokens), returning (number_admitted,tokens_used).
idea: A deterministic replay proves the admission arithmetic only. Actual tools still need authorization and outcome handling; provider usage, elapsed time and retries must be reconciled with the budget after every real operation.

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: Implement admitted_steps(costs,max_steps,max_tokens), returning (number_admitted,tokens_used). Nonnegative integer costs and budgets only. Stop at the first exceeded limit; zero-cost steps still consume a step.
